_meta: A list of dotted version strings, used to show why version numbers must be compared component-by-component as integers, not as strings, because a lexicographic (string) comparison orders them wrong: '1.10' sorts before '1.9' as text, since character by character '1.1' matches '1.' then '1' is less than '9', even though release 1.10 comes after 1.9. A version like '1.10.0' is not a number and not a word; it is a sequence of integer components separated by dots, and the correct ordering compares those components left to right as integers -- 1 vs 1, then 10 vs 9, where 10 > 9, so 1.10 > 1.9. A string comparison instead compares the raw characters, and character comparison is per-character: at the position where one version has '1' (the first digit of '10') and the other has '9', '1' < '9', so the whole string '1.10' is judged less than '1.9'. The bug is invisible while every component stays a single digit (string and numeric order agree up to 1.9), and appears the moment a component reaches double digits, which is exactly when a project has shipped enough releases to have a 1.10 -- so it tends to strike mature, widely-used software. The fix is to parse each version into a tuple of integers and compare the tuples. versions is the list of version strings to order. It is the fixture; the string-sorted order, the component-wise integer-sorted order, and the specific pair that the two disagree on are computed.
